banner.title: litellm-pgvector
banner.tagline: The stateless server behind LiteLLM's pgvector store, keeping every embedding in the shared Postgres 18 cluster.

explainer.title: Role, schema, then a stateless server

steps.title: Role
steps.text: The litellm-pgvector-db Kustomization creates the litellm_pgvector role and database on the shared postgres-18 cluster. Removing it keeps the data.
steps.scene: a key card issued for a locked room

steps.title: Schema
steps.text: A Job runs schema.sql as the superuser, creates the vector extension, then switches to the app role so the app owns its tables.
steps.scene: a table grid being drawn on a board

steps.title: Secrets
steps.text: Two ExternalSecrets feed the server its own connection string and API key, and the Job its superuser login. The server never sees the superuser password.
steps.scene: two sealed envelopes with separate keys

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: The stateless server answers OpenAI-style vector-store calls on port 8000. It has a ClusterIP Service and no HTTPRoute, so only LiteLLM reaches it.
steps.scene: a server rack behind a single door

steps.title: Embed
steps.text: The server embeds search queries with qwen3-embedding-8b through LiteLLM, requested at 2000 dimensions, and searches the stored vectors with an HNSW cosine index.
steps.scene: vectors arranged along a search line

art.about: a stateless vector store server that keeps embeddings in Postgres with an HNSW index and is reached only through a proxy
